newsitem.title: USA: Shuttle Columbia moves closer to launch.
newsitem.headline: Shuttle Columbia moves closer to launch.

text.p: The U.S. space shuttle Columbia was moved to its launch pad on Wednesday and was on schedule for blastoff, despite the last-minute replacement of two weak windows.
Columbia, NASA's oldest shuttle, made the six-hour, four-mile (6.4 km) crawl to the launch pad in readiness for the seventh and final shuttle flight of the year, tentatively scheduled for Nov. 8.
"We were able to replace the windows with relative ease and much quicker than initially forecast," said NASA spokesman Bruce Buckingham. "We remain on target for a Nov. 8 launch."
During Columbia's 16-day fight, its 21st voyage in space, two science satellites will be released and a pair of spacewalks are planned to test space station construction techniques.
